capability: Hansen 3-component (δ_d dispersion, δ_p polar, δ_h H-bond) chi baseline vs ML comparison for OMG chi 3-solvent. Third KPI for amphora-solvency-score, directly extending and improving my prior simplified 1-component Flory-Huggins receipt which had catastrophic R² = -207 to -5389. Hansen 1967/2007 formula: chi = V_s/(RT) × R_a²/4 + 0.34 with R_a² = 4(Δδ_d)² + (Δδ_p)² + (Δδ_h)². Group contribution for δ_d, δ_p, δ_h via Van Krevelen 1990 Ch. 7 + Beerbower 1984. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

metrics.name: hansen_pure_pearson_at_least_as_strong_as_hildebrand_within_noise_chloroform
metrics.note: Hansen 3-component pure |Pearson r| = 0.0760 vs Hildebrand 1-component pure |Pearson r| = 0.0779 for chloroform. Difference -0.0019, tolerance 0.01. HONEST FINDING: Hansen improves for water (0.125 vs 0.091, +37%) and ethanol (0.079 vs 0.072, +10%) — the polar/H-bonding solvents where the added components should help. For chloroform (the dispersion-dominated solvent with δ_p=3.1, δ_h=5.7 both LOW), Hansen slightly worsens (0.076 vs 0.078, −3%) — the polar/H-bond terms don't help when the solvent has near-zero polar and H-bond components anyway.
